newsitem.title: USA: Apple to rehire co-founder Jobs - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Apple to rehire co-founder Jobs - newspaper.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. is considering rehiring Steven Jobs -- the co-founder the company fired in 1985 -- to help update the Macintosh personal computer, the Los Angeles Times reported Friday.
The newspaper, citing unidentified sources, said Jobs will be hired as a part-time consultant and "technology guru" in charge of the software project.

Apple spokeswomen said the company does not have an announcement "at this time." A spokeswomen at Next Computers Inc., the company Jobs founded after he left Apple, also declined to comment. Jobs could not be reached for comment.

Apple has been in discussion with several software companies in recent weeks, looking for help in writing a brand-new version of the fundamental software that controls the Macintosh. The company needs an innovative operating system -- the program that controls the basic functions of the PC -- to keep its customers and software developers.
Jobs' software company, Next, offers an operating system with many of the software bells and whistles Apple needs to keep pace with PCs running Windows software from Microsoft Corp.
Jobs told The Wall Street Journal Monday that he was advising Apple on software development, but would not elaborate on his involvement.

Apple programmers working on the project said Chief Technical Officer Ellen Hancock has been discussing Apple's options with several software experts from outside companies, including Sun Microsystems Inc. and closely held Be Inc.
But the programmers said Friday that Hancock has yet to tell them what the operating system will look like or whether it will use technology from Next, Sun or Be.
Apple has a self-imposed deadline of Jan. 7 to reveal its operating system strategy at the MacWorld trade show.
